collection: IELTS Academic Listening Part 2 community garden practice
note: Original supervised listening practice. Keep examiner script, explanations and answers out of learner view. Recorded audio remains outstanding.

listeningSet.title: Welcome to Willow Garden
listeningSet.learnerInstructions: Questions 1–5. Match each activity to a feature. Choose one letter A–G for each activity. You may use a letter more than once. Questions 6–10. Complete each sentence with ONE WORD ONLY.

matchingOptions.A: Work is carried out in pairs.

listeningSet.examinerInstructions: Allow learners to read the prompts and matching list first. One reader delivers the complete monologue once at a natural pace. Award one mark per correct response. Accept letter case variations, but require correct spelling for sentence completions.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Good morning, and welcome to Willow Garden. I’m Mariam, the volunteer coordinator. This garden began as a patch of unused land behind the community hall. Local residents have gradually turned it into a place to grow food and learn practical skills. We now have several activities for new volunteers, so I’ll explain what each involves and then cover a few arrangements for your first visit.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: First, seed sowing takes place beside the greenhouse. You will learn how deeply to plant different seeds and how to label them. We provide all the materials, and at the end you can take your planted pot home. We hope watching it grow will encourage you to try the same method on a balcony or windowsill.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Compost care is more physical. Volunteers turn the material and check its moisture. This session cannot go ahead when heavy rain has made the working area too wet; in that case we move it to the following week. Please check our notice before leaving home.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: The pond survey is suitable for anyone who enjoys noticing small details. You won’t work alone. I allocate a partner to each volunteer so that two people can compare what they see and check the record together. You remain on the bank throughout.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Garden stories is our quietest activity. Although the name might suggest sitting under a tree, we hold it inside the old store building. There are chairs and a collection of photographs there. Long-standing residents share memories of how this neighbourhood has changed.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Finally, family planting is designed for children and the adults who bring them. We have short tools and raised beds. A parent or another responsible adult must stay with each child throughout the session. Our volunteers demonstrate the tasks but do not take over supervision.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Now for the practical arrangements. On your first visit, report to the reception desk rather than going directly to an activity. The receptionist will give you a green badge. Please keep it visible, as it tells our team that you have completed the welcome check.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Leave bags and any valuables in the lockers near reception. A bag on a path can easily be knocked over or become a tripping hazard. You keep the locker key with you while you work.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: At the tool station, someone will show you how to carry and return each tool. Tell the supervisor immediately if you notice damage. A damaged tool must have a red label attached and be put aside, so that nobody else picks it up before it is repaired.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: Before leaving, use the handwashing point. We supply soap as well as running water. A quick wipe with a tissue is not enough after handling soil, so allow time to wash properly.

examinerScript.speaker: Coordinator
examinerScript.line: We value your comments, too. There is a suggestion box by the exit. Put any written feedback in that box, even if it is only a few words. We read it at the weekly planning meeting and use it to improve future sessions. Thank you for giving your time to the garden.
